description: Tiny-Twin is a CPU-native, full-stack digital twin framework that enables realistic, repeatable 5G experimentation on commodity CPUs. It combines time-varying multi-tap convolution with a complete 5G protocol stack, supports plug-and-play replay of diverse channel traces, and provides built-in real-time RIC integration and per-UE channel isolation for testing network algorithms and protocol designs. The authors say a redesigned software architecture and system-level optimisations allow fine-grained convolution entirely in software, that it scales to multiple concurrent user equipments while preserving protocol timing and end-to-end behaviour, and that it is a middle ground between low-fidelity simulators and high-cost hardware emulators. Producer: Ali Mamaghani, Ushasi Ghosh, Srinivas Shakkottai, Dinesh Bharadia and Ish Kumar Jain, submitted 13 January 2026 and revised 5 May 2026. Coverage: radio access experiments at laboratory scale. Access: the abstract page was read; a repository link was not opened, so the release location is not verified. Licence and cost: the abstract states an open-source release; licence not stated for the software; the describing arXiv preprint is under the CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: an emulator of the radio access and protocol stack, not a model of network deployment or outage. Simulation uses: the twin supports testing of network algorithms under replayed channel conditions. Related record: the Open Wireless Digital Twin platform (platform-open-wireless-digital-twin-oai-sionna).
